title: The release gate races the asynchronous post-commit auto-capture: HEAD can move mid-gate
observation: RESOLVED by daffc71 (dec_290bf70a65) — this finding was still filed open but the fix had already shipped. tooling/release-gate.mjs:632-640 implements candidate fix (b): observeNormalizedSource() diffs gate-start HEAD against observed HEAD and, when every changed path passes isMemoryChurnPath (.hunch/** plus the five GROUNDING_DOC_PATHS), normalizes the observed commit back to the gate-start commit and records it in toleratedMemoryCommits. The receipt keeps commit_after as the RAW head for transparency and itemizes tolerated_memory_commits so a reader can audit exactly what rode in. statusWithoutMemoryChurn() does the same for working-tree dirt, keeping a rename fatal unless BOTH sides are churn. Anything touching real source still fails hard. Re-checked 2026-08-12 while about to re-implement it — querying the graph first would have been cheaper than reading the code.
evidence: tooling/release-gate.mjs:632-640 observeNormalizedSource() — HEAD-move tolerance gated on isMemoryChurnPath
